message.content:
Although a Leshy, Pebble Spring became immediately fascinated by the mortal settlements when they set foot in a city.
They loved the nicely paved ground, the intricate bridges, and, most of all, they loved houses.
The nicely laid out stone walls formed shelters from the weather yet connected the earth with the stories from every family.
They decided to learn the craft of housebuilding with the help of a touch of arcane magic from their self-made staff.
The first lesson was to measure every stone.
The second lesson was to mix the mortar slowly.
The third lesson was to listen to the wind.
A mason taught them how to cut the beams.
Another mason taught them how to shape the doors.
The staff hummed when the stones were true.
The paint came in green and amber shades.
The roof was covered with soft moss.
The garden had tiny stone lanterns.
The fence had curved branches woven through it.
The hearth was made of river rock.
The windows looked out over the quiet lane.
The neighbors smiled at the little carved birds.
The house smelled of honey, wood, and rain.
The village called it a home that breathed.
The first door opened with a soft click.
The second door opened with a gentle creak.
The third door opened into a sunny porch.
The whole street seemed to wake with color.
The Leshy artist painted the gables, the fences, the windows, the shutters, the garden gates, the little birds, the mossy paths, and the soft clouds until the entire house wore a soft, warm, and spotty coat.
